# NATIVE VALVE ENDOCARDITIS WITH STAPHYLOCOCCI

Endocarditis with Staphylococcus aureus and coagulase-negative staphylococci are

treated similarly.

Retrospective studies show that patients with native valve staphylococcal

endocarditis treated with valve replacement and antimicrobials have a lower

mortality rate than those treated with antimicrobials alone. Consult

cardiothoracic surgery for all patients with staphylococcal endocarditis.

Most patients need 6 weeks of antimicrobial treatment. For vancomycin-resistant

strains Infectious Disease consultation is recommended.

# Treatment for methicillin-susceptible strains

Preferred:

[Nafcillin 2 gm IV q4h \($$\) DI for 6 weeks](psjizid-nafcillin-2gm-iv-q4h)

Primary alternative:

[Assessment of beta-lactam reaction CLICK HERE](orzid2-gmenu-abx-beta-lactam-allergy-assesment)

Treat for 6 weeks:

[Cefazolin 2 gm IV q8h \($\) R](psjizid-cefazolin-2gm-ivpb-q8h)

Secondary alternative, after assessment of beta-lactam reaction above:

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R for 6 weeks](orz-set-abx-vanco-new-start-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)

# Treatment for methicillin-resistant strains

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R for 6 weeks](orz-set-abx-vanco-new-start-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)

< OR >

[Daptomycin 8-12mg/kg q24h \($$$$\) R,DI for 6 weeks](psjizid-daptomycin-8-12mg-kg-q24h)
